as_built: The canon's test of this claim was built and measured: the semilocal pointwise floor (floors.py Semilocal_Xc_Ridge_Features stacks the density, its spectral gradient magnitude and its Laplacian as per-point ridge features — the Savin/Tsirelson-style approximate ELF from the density alone) scores a unit-aggregated median mean absolute error of 0.0976 on the cubic block's fold 0, against 0.00217 for the flagship operator and 0.0160 for a positional training-mean template: a pointwise map from the density and its first two derivatives is 45x worse than the nonlocal operator and 6x worse than ignoring the input entirely, which is the measured content of 'not a lookup'. Spectral weights on a fixed Fourier mode set: kernels/spectral (full and factorized per-axis mode weights, mode truncation, spectral resampling), used by factorized_fourier (19 modes per axis at 40^3, evaluated on 80^3 at 0.62% self-consistency per operator-results.md I.1) and codomain_attention. Alias-free bandlimited design: compositions.MultiScale with exact spectral resampling plus the 'alias_free' Layer activation mode and compositions/activation.py machinery (alias_free_convolutional, parts built; the fused tile-streamed activation kernel is not built). The framework also tests the claim once at framework level (framework/invariance.py: resolution, supercell, size and symmetry axes with their nulls).

as_built: The suite's flagship task, charge density → electron localization field, is by the document's own account without a published precedent as that task: test-suite.md §2 records that the only existing ELF network maps geometry → ELF ('single element, pure NN, no operator structure') and offers V2Rho-FNO (potential → density) as 'adjacent' precedent for the pattern, while the archived operator-list.md states 'predicting the electron localization function from the true self-consistent DFT density has NEVER been published ... so this is OPEN'. as_built: No member trains a fine-grid ELF prediction and downsamples it. The flagship's training loss compares the coarse prediction with the coarse target directly (Localization_Loss: residual = predicted - targets at the 40^3 processing shape); the only fine->coarse operations are spectral truncation of the input fields (density, magnetization, potential) and the post-hoc super-resolution self-consistency check, which is an evaluation row, not training. codomain_attention works at the coarse grid throughout (the canon's own zero-pad-then-subsample recipe was simplified away); alias_free_convolutional states the law verbatim and places its head at the half scale; Downsampled_By_Two is used only inside the fused alias-free activation and the multi-scale composition, never on an ELF prediction.

as_built: principal_component: a rank-32 POD (PCA) of the raw training fields is the fixed output basis (FixedModeExpansion), and an MLP branch 6 -> 64 -> 64 -> 64 -> 32 maps parameters to the mode coefficients, trained by mean-squared error in coefficient space. as_built: canonical trains through PointSampledBatches: each step draws 8 runs with replacement and 4,096 fresh points inside each, Forward_Point_Values evaluates the trunk only at those points, and validation uses 512 evenly spaced points per run, so step memory scales with 8 x 4,096 points rather than the 64k-262k-point grids. The training fields themselves are held resident in single precision (232 MB for the strain training role). The fixed-basis pair trains in 32-dimensional coefficient space on one fixed batch and the energy trunk on one fixed whole-curve batch (under 5 MB); no configuration is O(grid) per step.

as_built: Ridge_Predictions fits a closed-form standardized ridge (regularization 1e-6, normal equations) from the spread-standardized run parameters to the rank-32 POD coefficients of the training fields (Project(basis, train.fields)) and reconstructs the field from the predicted coefficients; it is reported as ridge_floor and compared as ridge_to_coefficients in every strain and perovskite block.

as_built: TwoBranchEncoder holds a density branch (BasisProjectionEncoder onto a rank-32 POD basis of the two log-compressed spin densities, then SensorEncoder((32, 128, 128))) and a potential branch (BasisProjectionEncoder onto a rank-32 POD basis of the two mean-removed spin potentials, then SensorEncoder((32, 128, 128)), seeded one past); the two 128-wide latents are multiplied elementwise, one learned channel head (128 → 256) splits the product into two per-channel rows, and a shared BasisExpansion(128, (256, 256, 256)) trunk with a bounded 0–1 head reads them out over the localization grid. The twin is the same class with potential=None. The original manifest's kernel/composition entries (LowRankKernel / ExplicitStack) were corrected to no kernel / WithoutIntegralLayers, recorded in IMPLEMENTATION.md.
evidence: operators/multiple_input_operator_network/__init__.py: 'density_branch = SensorEncoder((density_rank, BRANCH_HIDDEN_WIDTH, LATENT_WIDTH), seed=seed)' / 'potential_branch = SensorEncoder((potential_rank, BRANCH_HIDDEN_WIDTH, LATENT_WIDTH), seed=seed + 1)' / 'readout = BasisExpansion(LATENT_WIDTH, TRUNK_HIDDEN_WIDTHS, PeriodicCoordinateFeatures(), OUTPUT_CHANNEL_LABELS, seed=seed + 3)'. report.md: 'Two `SensorEncoder((32, 128, 128))` branches over rank-32 proper-orthogonal coefficients of the log-compressed spin densities and of the mean-removed spin potentials, combined by an elementwise product in the shared 128-wide latent, split into two 128-wide per-channel rows by one learned channel head, read out by a shared `BasisExpansion(128, (256, 256, 256))` trunk with a bounded zero-to-one head.' as_built: Only the invariant variant is built, and it departs from the published invariant DeepDFT in three ways. (1) Each kernel's radial filter is a linear contraction of a 20-function sinc basis with a weight tensor of shape (basis, out, in); no filter-generating MLP is used. (2) The two phases run in sequence: 3 atom-only layers, then 3 joint layers where atoms keep updating, so atoms are updated 6 times and probes 3 times. In the paper, probes are updated at every interaction step from that step's atom states. (3) The parameter count is 523,970. The receive-only probe mechanism does match the commitment.
evidence: continuous.py: 'radial_weights': generator.normal(0.0, scale, size=(basis_count, output_channels, input_channels)); Forward: 'per_edge = profile_features[:, :, None] * sent_values[:, None, :] ... Scatter_Add ... Einstein_Summation("tbc,boc->to", accumulated, lifted["radial_weights"])'. Probe receive-only: message_passing.py 'sending_mask = combined_roles != PROBE_ROLE; kept_edges = sending_mask[combined_graph.sending_points]'; Test_Probes_Never_Send and Test_Probes_Never_Influence_Atom_Features pass (`pytest operators/tests/test_deep_dft.py` -> '16 passed in 13.46s'). The PaiNN variant is absent (see L4-006). The comparison with the paper's per-step probe updates and filter networks rests on the card's own words ('filter-generating MLPs') and on the paper's design as I recall it. as_built: Built as committed. Periodic_Radius_Graph folds each fractional gap to the nearest image, then enumerates images per axis with reach ceil(r_c / h_i), where h_i = V/|a_j × a_k| (Cell_Heights), and keeps a pair only if its distance is ≤ r_c. The reach suffices because round(x) ≤ ceil(x). A test checks the sheared-cell case.

as_built: The sinc radial basis of 20 functions under a cosine cutoff is built as committed. as_built: Built as committed. Per structure, half the probes are uniform in the fractional cell and half sit at a uniformly chosen atom plus an isotropic 3-D Gaussian offset (σ = 0.7 Å, drawn as a Cartesian 3-vector). The weights are 1/q(x), with q the mixture density summed over periodic images, and the loss is self-normalized by those weights.

as_built: deep_dft joins probe points to the atoms in one point set with roles; probes only receive messages (Sending_Points filters to atom-sourced edges), and probes can be placed anywhere in the cell. The output is a smooth function of probe position (sine basis under a cosine cutoff), but no derivative with respect to position is implemented or tested: the radial profile is computed in plain numpy, outside the autodiff engine.
evidence: Tests Test_Probes_Never_Send and Test_Probes_Never_Influence_Atom_Features exist. IMPLEMENTATION.md: 'Probe points placed anywhere in the cell join the message graph but only receive, so the density is a function queryable at any point and differentiable in position', and also 'The profile is pure geometry, computed once per phase on the host in plain numpy'.
